shower.thought: You'll never know if you have good taste or just got lucky a lot.
The people who hurt you most are usually the ones who showed you they cared first.
We call it "sleeping in" but you're really just finally getting the sleep you've owed yourself all week.
You've probably had a conversation that changed someone's life without realizing it.
The only reason you know your childhood wasn't that bad is because you survived it.
Most of what you're anxious about right now won't matter in five years, but you can't know which things those are.
You can't miss someone you've never met, yet you probably do.
Time moves slower when you're paying attention to it and faster when you're not—so boredom might be the only honest measure of time.
The worst part of losing something isn't the loss itself; it's the moment you reach for it out of habit and remember it's gone.
People spend money on things to impress people they don't actually like.
You're the villain in someone else's story and you'll never know why.
The things you do in private define you more than the things you do in public, but you're the only one keeping score.
Every song you love was written by someone who felt something you'll never fully understand, no matter how many times you listen.
You can't be truly spontaneous if you're thinking about being spontaneous.
The people who seem to have it all figured out have just gotten better at hiding their confusion.
Nostalgia is just heartbreak from the past that you're no longer living through.
You learn more from the person who argues with you than the person who agrees with you, which is probably why you avoid arguments.
The most honest moment between two people is often right after one of them admits they were wrong.
You'll spend decades becoming the person your younger self would respect, only to realize your younger self didn't know anything.
We treat our potential like it's infinite, but we're spending it like it's not.

darkjoke.thought:
I told my girlfriend she was drawing her eyebrows too high.
She looked surprised.

My therapist says I'm self-destructive.
I told her that's great feedback, but I'm not paying for it.

I have a stepladder because my real ladder left when I was young.
It's not a very good one.

My friend got hit by a bus last week.
He's fine now—they only hit him once.

I said to my doctor, "I think I'm paranoid."
He said, "Why would you think that?"
I said, "The way you said that."

Went to a funeral yesterday where they served the ashes mixed into a pasta dish.
I wouldn't recommend it, but you have to respect the commitment.

My girlfriend left me because I'm too pessimistic.
Knew that would happen.

I used to volunteer at a suicide hotline.
They said I wasn't a good fit because I kept asking, "Are you sure?"

My wife said I never listen to her.
At least that's what I think she said—I wasn't really paying attention.

The dentist told me I need to floss more.
I said, "That's not what you said when you were doing the autopsy on my last girlfriend."

I'm reading a book on anti-gravity.
I can't put it down.

My dad's in the hospital.
The doctors say he's in a stable condition.
I said, "Great! Can I ride him?"

My therapist asked me to describe my relationship with my parents.
I said, "Well, one's dead and the other wishes I was."
She said, "I'm sorry."
I said, "Don't be—I finally have something in common with them."

I told my wife she was acting paranoid.
She said, "Stop spreading rumors about me."

My boss said I'm not taking my job seriously.
I said, "That's fair," and quit on the spot.
He seemed shocked.
I said, "What? You said I should take it seriously."

I asked my dad why he never showed up to my baseball games.
He said, "Well, I'm showing up now."
I said, "Dad, I'm 32."
He said, "I know. Traffic was murder."

My girlfriend asked me if there was someone else.
I said, "No, babe, there's nobody else. Just me and my coping mechanisms."

I went to a birthday party for someone who was turning 100.
It was weird because nobody there believed he'd make it.
Turns out, they were right.

My accountant asked if I had any major expenses this year.
I said, "Yeah, turns out keeping my wife's family out of my life is priceless."

I told my friend his apartment was really depressing.
He said, "I know. I tried to jump out the window for fresh air."
I said, "How'd that go?"
He said, "Turns out I'm on the ground floor."
I said, "Well, that explains the broken ankles."
